title: #60 Don't Have the Title and Date on the Board During a Do Now
author: Barton, Craig
summary: Barton examines a small but consequential Do Now habit: leaving the title and date visible on the board while students are meant to be working through starter questions. Drawing on a recent school visit, he shows how students used the visible title and date as cover to stall -- slowly copying them down while appearing productive from the teacher's vantage point at the front -- even four minutes into the lesson. He notes this isn't fixable simply through better circulation, since that's difficult with large classes, and that some students genuinely copy slowly rather than deliberately stalling, so the behaviour isn't purely a discipline issue. His proposed fix is structural rather than behavioural: don't display the title and date during the Do Now at all, showing only the questions, and reveal the title and date afterward. He frames this as removing a "significant barrier to thinking" so the lesson can open with immediate cognitive engagement rather than a low-stakes copying task.
points: Even in a class that looks productive from the front of the room, students can use a visible title and date as legitimate-looking cover for stalling on real thinking during the Do Now.
The problem persists even with attentive teaching, since effective circulation is difficult with large classes and some students are simply slow copiers rather than deliberate stallers.
The fix targets the environment, not student behaviour directly: remove the title and date from the board during the Do Now and reveal them only afterward.
Barton frames the change as removing a "barrier to thinking," reframing a seemingly cosmetic board-management detail as a lever on how quickly a lesson achieves genuine cognitive engagement.
quotes: Some of these changes are substantial, but one is not: Don't have the title and date on the board during a Do Now.
The teacher had not picked up on this because, from his vantage point at the front of the classroom, it looked like the students were working. But they weren’t.
I see this all the time - students slowly copying down the date and title, happily putting off thinking for a few minutes.
Effective circulation can help, of course. But with large classes, this is tricky to do.
A more straightforward solution is not having the date and title on the board during the Do Now, just the questions.
This removes a significant barrier to thinking, allowing the lesson to get off to a productive start.
